name: TAT-12/13 erbium-amplified transatlantic ring
summary: A working North Atlantic cable ring with erbium-doped optical amplifiers in its submerged repeaters.
description: The TAT-12/13 consortium used erbium-doped fibre amplifiers in a ring linking the US, England and France. The transatlantic legs backed one another up and each transmitting fibre initially carried a single 5 Gb/s channel.

date.basis: CERN and the FCC inventory give 1996 for the TAT-12/13 system.

events.statement: The TAT-12/13 ring entered service as an optically amplified transatlantic system.
events.scope: Service date for the ring as a system, as reported by CERN.

evidence.locator: CERN/IT/97/5, “Current Cable Systems”, TAT-12 and TAT-13 paragraph
evidence.supports: CERN gives the 1996 operation date, optical amplifier configuration and routes.

evidence.locator: Optical Amplifiers and Their Applications, paper TO8, abstract
evidence.supports: AT&T author reports the use of EDFAs, two transatlantic legs and the single-channel configuration.

evidence.locator: Submarine Cable Systems table, TAT-12/13 row
evidence.supports: The independent regulatory inventory corroborates the 1996 service year.

links.statement: TAT-12/13 and the Bell Labs laboratory amplifier both used erbium-doped fibre to boost an optical signal directly.
links.scope: Optical gain principle. No component-level tracing from the experimental apparatus to the installed repeaters.

evidence.locator: Optics Letters 12(11), pp. 888–890, author affiliations, History and abstract
evidence.supports: Shows optical gain in erbium-doped single-mode fibre in the laboratory.

evidence.locator: Optical Amplifiers and Their Applications, paper TO8, abstract
evidence.supports: Reports erbium-doped fibre amplification in the deployed cable system.

evidence.locator: CERN/IT/97/5, “Current Cable Systems”, TAT-12 and TAT-13 paragraph
evidence.supports: The secondary CERN overview corroborates that TAT-12/13 used erbium-doped fibre optical amplifiers.
